# Themes {#ggplot2-themes}

## Introduction

:::{.callout-note}
## Why this matters

Themes take a correct plot to publication-ready: fonts, gridlines and background tuned once, reused everywhere.
:::

:::{.callout-warning}
## Common pitfall

Styling before the data mapping is right wastes effort; get geoms and scales correct first.
:::

In this chapter, we will learn to modify the appearance of all non-data 
components of the plot such as:

- axis
- legend
- panel
- plot area
- background
- margin
- facets

```{r load, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE, results='hide', message=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
```

## Basic Plot

We will continue with the scatter plot examining the relationship between 
displacement and miles per gallon from the mtcars data set.

```{r theme1, fig.align='center'}
p <- ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(disp, mpg))
p
```

## Style plot axes {#style-plot-axes}

### Style axis text {#style-axis-text}

We can use the `axis.title.x` argument to modify the appearance of the `X` 
axis. In the example below, we modify the color and size of the title using
the `element_text()` function. Remember, whenever you want to modify the
appearance of a theme element which is text, you must use `element_text()`.

You can use `axis.title.y` to modify the `Y` axis title. To modify the 
title of both axes together, use `axis.title`.

```{r theme2, fig.align='center'}
p + theme(axis.title.x = element_text(color = "red", size = 10, face = "italic"))
```

### Style axis ticks {#style-axis-ticks}

To modify the appearance of the axis ticks, use the `axis.ticks` argument. You can
change the color, linewidth and linetype of the ticks using the `element_line()`
function, and their length using `axis.ticks.length`.

```{r theme5, fig.align='center'}
p + theme(axis.ticks = element_line(color = 'blue', linewidth = 1.25, linetype = 2), 
          axis.ticks.length = unit(1, "cm"))
```

### Style axis lines {#style-axis-lines}

Use the `axis.line` argument to modify the appearance of the 
axis lines. You can change the color, linewidth and linetype of the line using
the `element_line()` function.

```{r theme6, fig.align='center'}
p + theme(axis.line = element_line(color = 'red', linewidth = 1.5, linetype = 3))
```

## Style the legend {#style-the-legend}

Now, let us look at modifying the non-data components of a legend.

```{r theme7, fig.align='center'}
p <- ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(disp, mpg, color = factor(cyl), shape = factor(gear)))
p
```

### Style the legend background {#style-legend-background}

We can modify the background of the legend using the `legend.background`
argument. You can change the background color, the border color and line type
using `element_rect()`.

```{r theme30, fig.align='center'}
p + theme(legend.background = element_rect(fill = 'gray', linetype = 3,  
          color = "black"))
```

### Style legend text {#style-legend-text}

We can modify the appearance of the text using the `legend.text` argument.
You can change the color, size and font using the `element_text()` function.

```{r theme34, fig.align='center'}
p + theme(legend.text = element_text(color = 'green', face = 'italic'))
```

### Style the legend title {#style-legend-title}

We can modify the appearance of the legend title using the 
`legend.title` argument. You can change the color, size, font and alignment
using `element_text()`.

```{r theme35, fig.align='center'}
p + theme(legend.title = element_text(color = 'blue', face = 'bold', hjust = 0.1))
```

### Move the legend position {#move-the-legend-position}

We can change the position and direction of the legend using:

- `legend.position`
- and `legend.direction`

```{r theme36, fig.align='center'}
p + theme(legend.position = "top", legend.direction = "horizontal")
```

## Apply a complete theme {#apply-a-complete-theme}

### Classic Dark on Light

```{r theme17, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(disp, mpg)) +
  theme_bw()
```

### Default Gray

```{r theme18, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(disp, mpg)) +
  theme_gray()
```

### Light

```{r theme19, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(disp, mpg)) +
  theme_light()
```

### Minimal

```{r theme20, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(disp, mpg)) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Dark

```{r theme21, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(disp, mpg)) +
  theme_dark()
```

### Classic

```{r theme22, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(disp, mpg)) +
  theme_classic()
```

### Void (Empty)

```{r theme23, fig.align='center'}
ggplot(mtcars) +
  geom_point(aes(disp, mpg)) +
  theme_void()
```

## Exercises

1. Apply `theme_minimal()` to a scatter plot.
2. Enlarge all text with `theme(text = element_text(size = 14))`.
3. Build a reusable custom theme and explain what it standardizes.
